kernelIdea: The complement of S ∩ T is S̄ ∪ T̄, and the complement of S ∪ T is S̄ ∩ T̄. These are the logic laws of 1.4 with ¬ ↔ complement, ∧ ↔ ∩, ∨ ↔ ∪.

kernels.l1: Outside both hoops is the same as outside this one and outside that one.
kernels.l2: The outside of the overlap is the outside of one hoop joined with the outside of the other. The outside of both hoops together is where the two outsides overlap.
kernels.l3: The outside of an intersection is the union of the outsides, and the outside of a union is the intersection of the outsides. Taking the outside swaps ∩ with ∪, exactly the way saying not swaps and with or.
kernels.l4: The complement of S ∩ T is S̄ ∪ T̄, and the complement of S ∪ T is S̄ ∩ T̄. These are De Morgan's logic laws with ¬ read as complement, ∧ as ∩, and ∨ as ∪.
kernels.l5: Complementation exchanges ∩ and ∪; each law is proved by double inclusion, with the logic law of 1.4 doing the work at the pivot.
kernels.l6: Complementing swaps ∩ and ∪ and reverses containment: the complement of S ∩ T is the union of the complements, and the other way round as well. These are Chapter 1's De Morgan laws carried over to sets, with the same proof underneath.
kernels.l7: Complementation exchanges intersection and union: the complement of S ∩ T is the union of the complements, and dually. The proof is a double inclusion whose pivot step is the logic law of §1.4.
kernels.l8: De Morgan for sets is the same identity as for connectives, because P(X) and the two-element Boolean algebra satisfy the same equational theory; the laws extend verbatim to indexed families via ¬∀ ≡ ∃¬.
